Using synchronous HTTP libraries like `requests` inside Python `async def` functions blocks the entire asyncio event loop! That means every other concurrent user is stuck waiting for your synchronous network call to finish.

Always use non-blocking HTTP clients like `httpx` or `aiohttp` with `await` in async code.

episode.title: The Echoing Exception
episode.hook: This monster crashes Node.js the second your API throws an error.
episode.logline: Express error handling middleware accidentally passes errors back to itself in an infinite call loop.
episode.topic: Express error handler calling next(err) indefinitely

beats.sub: When an error handler calls itself forever

beats.narration: The phone keeps ringing inside the error handler.

say.text: Ring ring! Forwarding error to the next handler!
Stop forwarding! You are the last error handler!

beats.narration: Calling next with an error in final middleware triggers infinite error loops.
beats.error: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded

beats.title: STACK OVERFLOW
beats.text: Express error middleware recursively called itself 10,000 times

beats.narration: The call stack overflows before any HTTP response is sent.

say.text: Hold on, I will call myself again!
Terminal error middleware must send a response!

beats.narration: End the error chain by returning an HTTP status and response body.
beats.note: Terminal error middleware must respond to the client rather than calling next(err)

beats.lesson: Never call next(err) in your final Express error handler without a next route.

In Express.js, passing an error into `next(err)` tells Express to find the next error handler middleware. If your final catch-all handler calls `next(err)`, Express loops back into the handler and overflows the stack.

episode.hook: Java's HashMap is not thread-safe and it will silently drop your data.

Separate get and put calls are not atomic!
